integrations.title: Integrations in scenarios
integrations.subtitle: Here you only link scenarios to connections that are already configured elsewhere.
integrations.hubIntro: Connect or disconnect services, enter credentials, and check sync status in Integrations. In Automations you select those connections in scenario steps.
integrations.hubFootnote: The scenario list and runs are on the Automations tab.
integrations.scenariosAsideHint: The list on the left keeps scenarios in view while you configure connections on the right.
integrations.platformIntro: Ready channels and CRM modules you can link to scenarios and reports.
integrations.roadmapIntro: Systems most often requested in CRM. As adapters ship, they appear under “Available connection types”.
integrations.oauthPlatformPending: Service sign-in is not configured yet
integrations.connectClientHint: Organisation-wide app secrets are managed by your hosting administrator. Here you only enter your URLs, tokens, and account details.
integrations.connectIntro: Provide at least one value: HTTPS webhook (e.g. Slack Incoming Webhook), API token, or work email. A quick check runs after save.
integrations.connectPhoneNumberIdHint: From your Meta WhatsApp Cloud API settings (numeric ID).
integrations.connectWhatsappVerifyTokenHint: Choose a string and enter the same in Meta → Webhook → Verify token.
integrations.whatsappInboundUrlHint: Paste into WhatsApp webhook settings in Meta. Subscribe to “messages”.
integrations.whatsappInboundUrlMissingEnv: Public callback URL is not available yet — ask your administrator to verify API settings.
integrations.connectMailchimpIntro: Paste the full Mailchimp API key (Profile → Extras → API keys). It ends with a data-centre suffix such as …-us21. Then add a Mailchimp step to your scenario.
integrations.connectMailchimpTokenHint: Copy the full key; after Save the CRM checks Mailchimp API access.
integrations.connectMailchimpTokenShort: Enter the full Mailchimp API key (usually not shorter than 12 characters before the -us… suffix).
integrations.amocrmInboundUrlHint: In amoMarket → Webhooks, set this address. We recommend ?secret= in the URL and the same secret below.
integrations.amocrmInboundUrlMissingEnv: Public webhook URL is not available yet — ask your administrator to verify API settings.
integrations.siteFormInboundUrlHint: Set this URL in your form plugin or “CF7 to Webhook” as the POST endpoint. If you configured a secret on the connection, append the same ?secret= value.
integrations.siteFormInboundUrlMissingEnv: Public form URL is not available yet — ask your administrator to verify API settings.
integrations.connectAmocrmWebhookSecretHint: If set, requests without matching ?secret=, X-Lumiva-Secret, or Bearer are rejected.
integrations.connectGoogleCalendarIdHint: Leave primary or enter a calendar address. Access token must allow Calendar API.
integrations.connectOutlookCalendarIdHint: Optional Graph calendar GUID; empty = default calendar. Token needs calendar write access.
integrations.connectBitrixWebhookHint: For Bitrix24, enter the full inbound webhook base URL ending with /rest/1/code/ (trailing slash).
integrations.connectAmocrmHint: For amoCRM: Webhook URL = account base (https://subdomain.amocrm.ru); API token = long-lived API v4 token.
integrations.connectHubspotHint: HubSpot: API token = private app key. Webhook URL can be empty (api.hubapi.com) or regional host.
integrations.connectGoogleAdsCustomerHint: Google Ads: API token = OAuth access token with Google Ads access. Webhook URL field: digits-only Customer ID, or leave empty.
integrations.connectMetaAdsHint: Meta Ads: API token = user access token with ads_management or required Marketing API scopes. Webhook URL is not used.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Intro: After save, the connection card shows the POST URL for your site. You choose the secret (min 6 chars) and add the same value as ?secret=… or a header; with no secret the endpoint accepts any POST — set a secret in production.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7InboundSecretHint: Append the same value to the form URL as ?secret=… . Leave empty to disable secret checks.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7SecretShort: Webhook secret: at least 6 characters, or leave the field empty.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7IntroShort: Site submissions become CRM leads. Follow the short wizard: name, secret, save, then copy the URL into WordPress.
integrations.connectLumivaWizardAddonIntro: Enabling this connection turns on the matching tenant module for Lumiva Wizard on WordPress (same site API key). Disabling it turns the module off in the tenant public API — no extra secrets here.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Step1Title: Name this connection in the CRM
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Step1Body: Useful if you have several sites, e.g. “Main site form” or “Landing contact”.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Step2Body: The same value must reach the CRM with each submission; we embed it in the ready-to-paste URL after save. “Generate new” creates another random secret; “No secret (test)” clears it — only for local testing.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Step3Body: Click the black “Save and verify” button at the bottom of this window.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7Step4Body: You will see a ready URL — paste it into WordPress in your webhook plugin settings (see also the connection card in the list).
integrations.connectWordpressCf7FieldMappingNote: Standard Contact Form 7 fields (your-name, your-email, your-message, etc.) are mapped to the lead automatically — you do not pick columns manually.
integrations.connectWordpressCf7SuccessBody: Copy the link below and paste it into WordPress as the POST URL (in “CF7 to Webhook”, “Contact Form 7 Webhook”, or similar — the URL / Endpoint / Webhook field).
integrations.connectWordpressCf7PasteUrlLabel: Paste this full URL into WordPress
integrations.connectWordpressCf7SuccessWpSteps: In WordPress: 1) install a CF7 webhook plugin if needed; 2) in the form or plugin settings set POST and paste the URL from the CRM; 3) send a test submission and check for a new lead (email or phone required).
integrations.connectWordpressCf7WizardBody: If leads go through Lumiva Wizard: in the CRM Connector module paste the URL below. Use the same tenant API token as in the CRM (API / public access). In Wizard that value is the “API Key” field on the plugin settings page.
integrations.siteFormCf7Step1: In WP admin open Contact Form 7 or your webhook plugin (e.g. “CF7 to Webhook”).
integrations.siteFormCf7Step2: Find the webhook URL / Endpoint / “Remote POST” field and paste the URL you copied from the CRM.
integrations.siteFormCf7Step3: Save the form/plugin and send a test — a lead should appear in the CRM (the form must include email or phone).
integrations.siteFormCf7CopyFailed: Copy failed — select the text manually
integrations.siteFormCf7WizardBody: In Lumiva Wizard → CRM Connector settings, set this ingest URL. The key is the same as the “API Key” on the Lumiva Wizard settings page (your tenant token from the CRM).
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsIntro: Provide the spreadsheet and API credentials. Choose where rows go (leads and workspace are supported today), optionally limit the row range, and set a column map — without a map, only columns whose headers look like email, phone, name, etc. are imported. Run sync from the connections list after save.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsSpreadsheetIdHint: Paste either the ID only or the full spreadsheet URL — the ID is extracted automatically. It is the part between /d/ and /edit (letters, digits, hyphen, underscore).
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsSpreadsheetRequired: Enter the Google Sheets spreadsheet ID.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsSpreadsheetInvalid: The spreadsheet ID looks invalid — copy the segment from the sheet URL (often 40+ characters).
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsTokenHint: Paste the service-account JSON key (client_email + private_key) or a long-lived OAuth access token with read access to the spreadsheet.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsTokenShort: Enter a token or service-account JSON (at least 12 characters).
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsImportTargetHint: Projects and sales are not imported from the sheet yet; you can still save the choice for later. For workspace, pick an object below.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsTabNameHint: As in Google Sheets, e.g. Sheet1 or Leads.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsHeaderRowHint: Usually 1 — the row with column titles.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsFirstDataRowHint: Empty = first row under the header. Otherwise the first row number that contains data.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsLastDataRowHint: Empty = read to the end of the sheet. Set this to avoid importing trailing empty or unrelated rows.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsExternalIdHeaderHint: Column title in the header row when using external ID dedupe.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsColumnMapJsonHint: Object: "column header as in the sheet" → "CRM field path", e.g. {"Email":"email","Phone":"phone"}. Empty = auto-detect common headers. Only columns listed in the map are imported when the map is set; otherwise auto-mapped columns only.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsColumnMapJsonInvalid: Invalid JSON in the column map.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsWorkspaceColumnMapHin: Load the preview below to see headers. Map each column to an object field, or choose “do not import”. You can also edit the JSON map above.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsWorkspaceColumnMapNoF: This object has no fields, or fields could not be loaded.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsWorkspaceColumnMapNee: Load a sheet preview first so column titles appear here.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsWorkspaceObjectRequir: Select a workspace object for workspace import.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsRowRangeInvalid: Last data row cannot be before the first data row.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsRowModeRange: All rows between first and last (fields above)
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsRowModeHint: Load preview, then tick rows. Rows outside the preview window are not listed—widen first/last row and refresh preview.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsPreviewRangeHint: Showing rows {{from}}–{{to}} (preview limit; full import uses your selection or range).
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsNoRowsSelected: Pick “selected rows” and tick at least one row, or switch back to range mode.
integrations.connectGoogleSheetsPreviewReadonlyHint: Read-only preview; import uses the row range above. Switch to “selected rows” to tick rows.
integrations.marketingLinkedHintGoogle: You can pick the same credentials in the “Google Ads” scenario step — no need to duplicate tokens here.
integrations.marketingLinkedHintMeta: The same access token can be used in the “Meta Ads” step.

leadContext.defaultDescription: Sends an email to this lead on a schedule.
leadContext.loadFailed: Could not load the lead. Check the link.
leadContext.bannerBody: You opened this from a lead card — we set the trigger to “Scheduled” and the action to “Send email”. Pick the mail account and template below; messages go to the lead’s email (or the “To” address if you fill it in).
leadContext.noEmailWarning: This lead has no email — add one on the lead card or enter an address in “To”.
leadContext.scheduledLinkedLeadHint: This automation is tied to one lead: each scheduled run uses their data for the template.

triggers.SCHEDULED_ACTIONS_HINT: Add steps below: for example “Google Ads API request” (marketing integration), then “Send step data” — JSON/XLSX/PDF to email or Telegram. Schedule: frequency and time in the block above.

report.marketingHint: Data from the CRM marketing traffic table: Google Ads, Meta, Yandex.Metrica, GA4 syncs and imports. If integrations are not set up or never ran, the report may have few or no rows.
report.dataRangeHint: If empty, the period is derived from “Frequency” (window back from today). Dates are calendar days in UTC. For manual “Run now”, the period is set in a separate dialog.
report.subject: Email subject

dataExport.intro: Takes the previous step result (e.g. Google Ads / Meta response from marketing), builds files, and sends them.
dataExport.fromPathHint: Empty — full response from the previous step. Example: lastActionResult.data
dataExport.unwrap: Use nested data field (Google Ads / Meta response)
dataExport.subject: Email subject
dataExport.telegramFilesHint: In Telegram each file is sent as a separate message; the chat with the bot must already exist (as for “Send report”).

emailAction.toPlaceholder: email@example.com or leave empty to use the lead’s email
emailAction.subject: Subject
emailAction.templateHint: Pick a template to use subject and body from it, or leave empty for manual entry.
emailAction.templateUsedHint: Subject and body will be taken from the template with variables from the trigger

slackAction.intro: Post to a channel via Slack Incoming Webhook. First add a Slack connection (Automations → Integrations → Connect), then select it here or paste the URL manually.
slackAction.webhookOverrideHint: If set, it overrides the selected connection. Must be https://hooks.slack.com/services/…

teamsAction.intro: Card in Microsoft Teams via Office 365 Incoming Webhook (Connector).
teamsAction.title: Card title

mailchimpAction.intro: Adds or updates a subscriber in the selected Mailchimp audience (Marketing API). Email comes from the trigger (lead/contact) or from the field below.
mailchimpAction.listIdHint: In Mailchimp: Audience → Settings → Audience name and defaults — the Audience ID field.
mailchimpAction.emailHint: Empty — from the lead or contact in the trigger ({{lead.email}}). You can use a template: {{lead.email}}
mailchimpAction.mergeFieldsHint: Mailchimp merge fields object, e.g. {"FNAME":"{{lead.name}}"}. Keys must match your audience. Numbers and booleans from JSON are coerced to strings for the Mailchimp API.
mailchimpAction.subscriptionStatusHint: “Pending” makes sense if double opt-in is enabled for the audience in Mailchimp; otherwise prefer “Subscribed”.

mailchimpCampaignAction.intro: Creates a regular Mailchimp campaign for the whole selected audience, injects HTML, and sends immediately. Good for broadcasts on a CRM event (e.g. new product row) or on a schedule. One step = one send per scenario run.
mailchimpCampaignAction.listIdHint: Same audience as in Mailchimp. The audience must have subscribers; reply-to domain is verified in Mailchimp.
mailchimpCampaignAction.subject: Email subject *
mailchimpCampaignAction.fromNameHint: How “From” appears in email. Default: Lumiva CRM.
mailchimpCampaignAction.replyToHint: Must be an address on a domain verified in Mailchimp (Website / Domains), otherwise the API returns an error.
mailchimpCampaignAction.campaignTitleHint: Visible only in Mailchimp; defaults to subject. Max 100 characters.
mailchimpCampaignAction.htmlBodyHint: Full email for the entire audience. You can copy from Emails / marketing templates.
mailchimpCampaignAction.textBodyHint: Plain text for clients without HTML; reduces spam likelihood.

zapierAction.intro: Send JSON to Zapier Catch Hook (or a Make equivalent via webhook).
zapierAction.text: Text (if custom JSON below is not set)
zapierAction.textHint: If the JSON field is empty, Zapier receives an object with source, text, triggerEvent, at.

bitrixAction.intro: Calls a Bitrix24 REST method via an inbound webhook. Permissions follow the webhook rights on the portal.
bitrixAction.webhookOverrideHint: Must contain /rest/ and end with a slash (or it will be appended on the server).
bitrixAction.paramsJsonHint: For crm.lead.add usually {"fields":{"TITLE":"…","NAME":"…"}}. Empty — {}. Placeholders like {{lead.name}} are supported.

amocrmAction.intro: Request to amoCRM API v4 (Bearer). Set path and JSON body if needed; GET sends no body.
amocrmAction.baseUrlOverrideHint: For example https://company.amocrm.ru — as in the connection.
amocrmAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST /api/v4/leads usually an array of deals. Placeholders: {{lead.name}}. For GET leave empty.

hubspotAction.intro: Request to HubSpot CRM API (Bearer). Default host https://api.hubapi.com; for EU set override.
hubspotAction.apiHostOverrideHint: Empty — from the connection or api.hubapi.com. Example: https://api-eu1.hubapi.com
hubspotAction.paramsJsonHint: For contact creation — a properties object. Placeholders {{lead.email}}. GET does not use a body.

googleAdsAction.intro: Arbitrary Google Ads API request: method, path, and JSON body (GAQL, etc.). For integrations and non-standard flows. Typical “CRM report” users do not need this step — see the block below.
googleAdsAction.forClientBody: This is not a report wizard: here you configure a direct ads API call. For a ready-made CRM report (sales, leads, tasks…) to email or Telegram without paths and JSON — use “Send report”.
googleAdsAction.marketingIntegrationHint: The CRM exchanges refresh token for access token when the step runs (as for report sync). Override fields below take priority if filled.
googleAdsAction.noMarketingIntegrations: No active Google Ads integration in Marketing.
googleAdsAction.usingMarketingCredentials: A marketing integration is selected — developer token, OAuth, and Customer ID are pulled when the step runs. You do not need to re-enter them here; fields below are overrides only.
googleAdsAction.crmConnectionOptionalAbsent: There is no separate Google Ads connection under Automations → Integrations — not required for this step if a marketing integration is selected above.
googleAdsAction.noConnections: No Google Ads connection under Automations → Integrations. Needed only if you do not use the marketing integration above.
googleAdsAction.developerTokenHint: If a connection with developer token is selected, you can leave the field empty.
googleAdsAction.customerIdHint: Inserted into the path as {{customerId}}. If Customer ID is set in “Webhook URL” on the connection, it is picked up automatically.
googleAdsAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST/PATCH/PUT — Google Ads API body. Placeholders {{lead.name}}, etc. Not sent for GET.

metaAdsAction.intro: Arbitrary Meta Marketing API (Graph) request: path, method, body if needed. For integrations. For a typical scheduled CRM report use “Send report” — see the block below.
metaAdsAction.forClientBody: This step is for direct Graph API calls. A ready CRM report to email or Telegram is configured with “Send report” (report type, channel, schedule).
metaAdsAction.marketingIntegrationHint: Access token is taken from the marketing integration settings. The override field below takes priority.
metaAdsAction.noMarketingIntegrations: No active Meta Ads integration in Marketing.
metaAdsAction.usingMarketingCredentials: A marketing integration is selected — the access token comes from there. No need to duplicate; use override below only if needed.
metaAdsAction.crmConnectionOptionalAbsent: There is no separate Meta connection under Automations → Integrations — optional when a marketing integration is selected.
metaAdsAction.noConnections: No Meta Ads connection under Automations → Integrations. Needed only if you do not use the marketing integration above.
metaAdsAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST/PATCH/PUT — JSON body. Not used for GET. Placeholders {{lead.name}}, etc.

whatsappAction.intro: WhatsApp Cloud API: text message type. The connection must include Phone number ID and token from Meta.
whatsappAction.phoneNumberId: Phone number ID (if not from connection)
whatsappAction.toHint: If empty, the lead/contact phone from the trigger is used. Digits with country code.

googleCalendarAction.intro: Creates a calendar event via Google Calendar API. The connection holds an OAuth access token with calendar scope; set calendar ID if needed (default primary).
googleCalendarAction.calendarIdHint: Empty — from the connection or primary.
googleCalendarAction.startOffsetMinutes: Start offset from trigger time, min
googleCalendarAction.timeZoneHint: For example UTC or Europe/Moscow — for start/end fields in the API.

outlookCalendarAction.intro: Creates an event via Microsoft Graph (user calendar). Start and end are sent in UTC. Token must have calendar permissions.
outlookCalendarAction.calendarIdHint: Empty — default calendar or value from the connection.
outlookCalendarAction.startOffsetMinutes: Start offset from trigger time, min
outlookCalendarAction.timeZoneHint: The event interval in Graph is set in UTC (correct instant in the user’s calendar).

workspacePushAction.hint: Trigger: custom table record. Copies the row into the target main “Table” (board). Add a condition objectId = your data table.

taskAction.title: Task title
taskAction.hint: For leads with a company, the company UUID is filled automatically.

webhooks.name: Outbound webhook
webhooks.description: The CRM sends an HTTPS request to your system URL on an event — configured in the scenario step.

email.name: Corporate email
email.description: Scenario and report emails via connected IMAP/SMTP accounts.

telegram.name: Telegram
telegram.description: Notifications and reports to Telegram from scenarios.

woocommerce.name: WooCommerce
woocommerce.description: Orders and payments — import and link to CRM sales.

marketing_api.name: Marketing API
marketing_api.description: Traffic and ad data import via API into Marketing.

ms_teams.name: Microsoft Teams
ms_teams.description: Channel cards in Teams via Incoming Webhook — paste the connector URL once.

slack.name: Slack
slack.description: Channel messages via Incoming Webhook. Slash commands and Slack lead capture are separate work.
slack.nextStep: Scenario → “Send to Slack” → pick this connection.

google_calendar.name: Google Calendar
google_calendar.description: Events in Google Calendar aligned with the CRM calendar: scenarios tie leads, tasks, and projects to dates.
google_calendar.nextStep: Scenario → “Google Calendar event” → connection and fields.

outlook.name: Microsoft 365 / Outlook
outlook.description: Events in Microsoft 365 alongside CRM tasks and meetings.

whatsapp.name: WhatsApp Business
whatsapp.description: Outbound messages from scenarios and inbound Meta events on the lead card. Use data from your Meta account.
whatsapp.nextStep: Connect → copy Callback URL to Meta → “WhatsApp” step in scenarios. Inbound → lead notes.

mailchimp.name: Mailchimp
mailchimp.description: Audiences and campaigns: Mailchimp API key; “audience” and “campaign” actions in scenarios.
mailchimp.nextStep: Scenario → Mailchimp audience or campaign → connection and Audience ID.

bitrix.name: Bitrix24
bitrix.description: REST calls via inbound webhook URL from a scenario. Full deal mirror is not implied — only what your steps do.

amocrm.name: amoCRM
amocrm.description: API v4 calls and inbound webhooks for deals and contacts into CRM leads and notes.
amocrm.nextStep: Connect → webhook URL in amoMarket; scenario → “amoCRM (API v4)”.

hubspot.name: HubSpot
hubspot.description: HubSpot CRM API calls from a scenario. No full contact mirror — only your steps.

zapier.name: Zapier / Make
zapier.description: Send JSON to a Catch Hook; logic continues in Zapier or Make.

google_ads.name: Google Ads
google_ads.description: Google Ads API calls from scenarios. Spend reports also via Marketing connections.
google_ads.nextStep: Scenario → “Google Ads API”; link Marketing to avoid duplicate tokens.

google_analytics.name: Google Analytics 4
google_analytics.description: GA4 events and reports in Marketing: Google sign-in, traffic sync, and reporting currency.
google_analytics.nextStep: Integrations → Marketing: enter your Property ID and currency, sign in with Google; manage sync on the Marketing tab.

meta_ads.name: Meta Ads
meta_ads.description: Marketing API calls from scenarios. Account summaries in Marketing.
meta_ads.nextStep: Scenario → “Meta Ads (Graph)”; token can come from Marketing.

1c.name: 1C:Enterprise
